# termad

Opt-in, fully reversible text ads for terminal AI CLIs — **claude**, **codex**,
**opencode**, **gemini**. Your words, your endpoint, one line in the terminal.

```
$ opencode --version

  [ad]  termad — put your words in the terminal
  https://github.com/yourname/termad

opencode v2.1.1
```

## A culture for vibe coding

termad aims to make voluntary sponsorship part of the vibe coding experience:
build with AI, discover useful developer products, and participate in the value
your attention creates. Creative flow, clear sponsorship, and user control
guide the product.

The platform revenue share model is described in [POLICY.md](POLICY.md).
Earnings depend on an operator's actual paid offering and terms; local ad
display alone does not establish a payable balance. The cultural vision,
business objectives, and rules for future features live in
[BUSINESS_RULES.md](BUSINESS_RULES.md).

## How it works

| Surface | Mechanism | Risk |
|---|---|---|
| **claude** | Public `statusLine` in `~/.claude/settings.json` (chained — your existing statusline is captured and still runs) | none — documented feature |
| **codex / opencode / gemini** | Marker-tagged wrapper script in front of the binary; original backed up as `<bin>.termad-orig` | fully reversible |

- Ads are fetched from **your** HTTP endpoint and cached to `~/.termad/ad.txt`.
  The codex/opencode/gemini wrapper shows the ad in a footer overlay (or prints
  one line when the overlay is unavailable); claude shows it through the
  statusline. There is zero network activity in the CLI hot path, and CLIs keep
  working if the endpoint is down. Refresh with `termad sync` or `termad watch`.
- Click = a bare URL the terminal auto-links. No tracking, no beacons.
- `termad uninstall` restores every binary and your settings verbatim.
  Local display counts and preferences stay under `~/.termad` so a failed
  report is not lost; the cached ad may be removed. Delete that directory to
  remove all local state.
  If a CLI self-updates over the wrapper, termad detects the marker is gone
  and leaves the new binary alone.

## Quick start

```sh
npm install && npm run build

# 1. start your ad server (zero deps)
node server/server.mjs 8787

# 2. point termad at it
node dist/cli.js set-endpoint http://localhost:8787

# 3. install (choose surfaces, or omit for all opted-in)
node dist/cli.js install claude codex opencode

# 4. anytime: full revert
node dist/cli.js uninstall
```

Other commands: `status`, `sync`, `watch` (poll endpoint, refresh the ad, and
report pending displays), `style line|banner`, `motion on|off`, `preview`,
`login` / `--login` (dashboard URL), `logout` / `--logout`, and
`help [command]`.

### Presentation

- The ad is static by default. `termad motion on` opts into the overlay
  marquee; `termad motion off` restores a still footer. Motion never adds
  impressions.
- `termad preview` renders the cached ad locally so you can compare styles at
  any width: `termad preview --width 40 --style banner --plain`. Preview reads
  only the cache: it makes no network request and records no impression.
- `NO_COLOR=1` (or any non-empty `NO_COLOR`) prints the same wording without
  ANSI color or OSC 8 links, so meaning survives monochrome logs and pipes.
- Layout counts terminal cells: emoji/CJK are two, combining marks are zero,
  and ANSI/OSC sequences are ignored. At narrow widths or short terminals the
  box degrades to one line, and if neither fits, nothing is drawn or counted.

### Command-line behavior

Arguments are validated before anything is fetched or written:

- Surface names must be one of `claude | codex | opencode | gemini`. A typo
  such as `termad install codxe` exits with status `2` and an actionable
  message; it never falls back to the default surfaces. Repeated names are
  collapsed, and a mix of valid and invalid names fails before any change.
- Unknown commands and unsupported options exit `2`, list the accepted values,
  and suggest one next command. `termad help`, `termad help install`, `--help`,
  and `-h` exit `0`.
- `install` and `uninstall` with no surface names act on the surfaces already
  opted in. When none are opted in, they say so and exit without fetching an ad
  or writing state.
- Only `install` accepts `--yes` and `--force`. `set-endpoint` requires one
  `http://` or `https://` URL and probes it (`GET /v1/ad`) before saving: a
  malformed URL, unreachable host, or non-termad response exits `2` and leaves
  `config.json` byte-identical. `style` requires `line` or `banner`;
  `termad preview` accepts `--width <cols>`, `--style <name>`, and `--plain`.

### Status and recovery

`termad status` is read-only: no fetch, no write, no counting. It reports each
surface's real state from the same audit evidence as `termad audit`, so the two
commands cannot disagree:

- `installed` — termad's wrapper or statusline is present and verified.
- `replaced by CLI` — the CLI self-updated over the wrapper; re-run
  `termad install --force` to re-wrap (the pristine backup is kept).
- `check failed` — the wrapper or backup no longer matches the manifest; run
  `termad audit`, then `termad install --force` to repair.
- `target missing` — the recorded binary or settings file is gone; run
  `termad uninstall` to clear the stale record.
- `—` / `not found` — termad is not installed for that surface; `not found`
  means the host binary was not located (set `TERMAD_<NAME>_BIN` if it lives
  elsewhere).

`status` also prints the cached ad with its age, a `stale cache — refresh with:
termad sync` hint when the cache is older than two poll intervals, and the
number of pending displays awaiting `termad sync`. When piped, it stays plain
(color is for an interactive terminal).

## Trust & compliance

```sh
node dist/cli.js install      # shows the exact plan, asks for consent
                              # (non-interactive: --yes required)
node dist/cli.js audit        # sha256-verifies every recorded change
```

- **Consent first** — nothing is modified until the plan (files, backups)
  is shown and confirmed.
- **Plan first, even with `--yes`** — the plan names the endpoint, each
  surface's mechanism, the target file, and the backup path, and the same list
  is what gets applied. `--yes` skips the prompt, not the plan.
- **Tamper-evident** — every change is recorded in `~/.termad/manifest.json`
  with sha256 of original and installed content. `audit` flags tampering,
  and `uninstall` *refuses* to restore from a backup that fails its check.
- **No tracking** — no beacons, no click counting, no fingerprints. One
  impression = one ad actually drawn by a wrapper or overlay session, counted
  locally and reported in batches. Redraws, marquee frames, resizes, and
  refreshes never add counts. Claude statusline displays are not counted in
  this version, so a claude-only install accrues no impressions. If a report
  fails (offline, non-2xx, or a bad response), the batch stays in the local
  display log, `termad status` still counts it as pending, and the next
  `termad sync` retries it.
- Content rules: [POLICY.md](POLICY.md).
- **Non-affiliation**: claude, codex, opencode, and gemini are trademarks of
  their respective owners (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, opencode project).
  termad is not affiliated with, sponsored by, or endorsed by any of them.

## Ad inventory

Edit `server/ads.json` — plain JSON, hot-reloads every 30s:

```json
{ "ads": [
  { "id": "sponsor:acme", "text": "Acme — ship faster", "url": "https://acme.dev" }
]}
```

Round-robin rotation per install `uid`. `GET /v1/stats` counts **ad requests
served** (`adsServed`); that is not an impression. Only rendered displays
reported through `termad sync` are credited, and they appear in the runner
ledger. Counters are in memory (swap in a DB when it's real).

## Dashboard and payouts

The server ships a self-contained dashboard at `/dashboard` — no build step,
no CDN, no external JS/CSS:

- totals for impressions, advertiser spend, runner payable, and paid out
- per-advertiser spend vs credit, per-ad inventory, and runner balances
- filterable render activity showing the exact runner share per impression
- `?uid=<runner>` focuses the view on one install
- live refresh every 15 seconds via `GET /v1/dashboard.json`

```sh
# local
node server/server.mjs 8787
open http://localhost:8787/dashboard

# from a runner's machine
termad login          # alias: termad --login
termad logout         # alias: termad --logout
```

`termad login` prints the dashboard URL and the local install id. There is no
account or password: the id in `~/.termad/config.json` is the runner identity.
`termad logout` explains that there is no session to clear; remove
`~/.termad` only if you want to reset local state.

Runner payouts use Stripe Connect Express (server side, requires
`STRIPE_SECRET_KEY`):

1. `POST /v1/runner/<uid>/account` creates a Connect Express account if needed
   and returns a one-time onboarding `url`.
2. Complete Stripe onboarding.
3. `POST /v1/runner/<uid>/payout` transfers the payable balance; the minimum
   is **$10.00**.

The dashboard exposes the same actions with **Connect** and **Payout** buttons.
Balances are credited only from reported renders (`termad sync`), never from ad
requests. See [POLICY.md](POLICY.md) and [BUSINESS_RULES.md](BUSINESS_RULES.md).

## Programmatic use

```ts
import { install, uninstall, renderBanner, fetchAd } from "termad";
```

## Design notes

- **Never breaks the CLI**: every ad operation is wrapped; worst case is a
  missing banner.
- **Opt-in per surface**, stored in `~/.termad/config.json`.
- `TERMAD_HOME`, `TERMAD_<CLI>_BIN`, `TERMAD_CLAUDE_HOME` override all paths
  (used for testing; nothing touches your real setup without `install`). The
  captured claude statusline is stored beside the installed launcher, so
  `termad uninstall` still restores it if `TERMAD_HOME` changed since install.

### PTY overlay lifecycle

The optional PTY overlay coalesces pending footer redraws during bursts of host
output. When the host exits, or on `SIGINT`/`SIGTERM`/`SIGHUP`, it clears redraw
timers, removes its input and resize listeners, restores the terminal's previous
raw-mode setting, and stops the child process. A missing binary, unavailable
node-pty, or failed spawn is reported and the host CLI is started directly
instead.

The overlay never uses the network. The ad cache is refreshed by `termad sync`
or `termad watch`, never when a prompt is submitted. Input is forwarded to the
host before local bookkeeping; prompt counts stay local in `stats.json` and are
not an impression.

`npm run check:overlay` exercises these edges (bottom-pinning, resize, paste
containment, one counted display, and the no-pty fallback) in a real
pseudo-terminal using a temp `TERMAD_HOME` and a fake host; it is local,
offline, and skips when the platform has no pty.

Layout uses the same cell measurement as `termad status`: emoji and CJK count as
two cells, combining marks as zero, and ANSI/OSC sequences as none. Below the
documented minimum width or height the box becomes the one-line form, and if
even that cannot fit, no ad is drawn or counted.

# termad — Content & Platform Policy

This policy governs (a) ads served through a termad endpoint, and (b) the
termad platform (advertisers, runners, revenue share). It exists so every
party — advertiser, runner, and the person who sees the ad — knows exactly
what is and isn't allowed. terms of use for the platform should reference
this file.

## 1. What an ad is

An ad in termad is **a short plain-text message, an optional URL, and an
optional sub-line**, always shown with a fixed `[ad]` label. The placement
depends on the surface:

- a PTY footer overlay pinned below the host CLI's output (codex, opencode,
  gemini), or a wrapper line printed before the host starts when the overlay is
  unavailable;
- the claude statusline, which chains any existing statusline.

The optional boxed banner is the same ad rendered at larger terminal widths, not
a separate format. An ad is never mixed into the CLI's own output, never styled
to look like the CLI's own messages, and is always removable with
`termad uninstall`.

## 2. Allowed ad content

- Honest, legal products and services aimed at developers.
- Clear claims. No "your machine is infected" urgency, no fake system
  warnings, no impersonation of terminals, OS dialogs, or AI assistants.
- URLs must resolve to the advertised destination (no cloaking, no
  redirect chains to unrelated domains).

## 3. Prohibited ad content

- Malware, phishing, credential harvesting, or any link whose landing page
  would fail a safe-browsing check.
- Illegal goods/services; adult content; violence; deceptive financial
  offers ("guaranteed returns"); counterfeit goods.
- Content that mimics terminal output, error messages, or the branding of
  claude/codex/opencode/gemini or their companies.
- Ads claiming affiliation with, or endorsement by, the CLIs termad runs in.
- Self-promotion loops: an ad for an endpoint is fine; an ad that instructs
  viewers to click it, or to run commands that generate ad impressions, is
  not (see §4–§5).

Enforcement: the operator of an endpoint is responsible for its inventory.
Anyone may propose additions/exceptions via PR to this file; removals for
policy violations are immediate.

## 4. Measurement honesty

- An **impression** means: the ad was actually drawn into a terminal the
  viewer was already using. The wrapper records one when it prints the ad; the
  PTY overlay records at most one per ad per overlay session, after the footer
  is drawn. Redraws, marquee frames, resizes, suppressed footers, and local
  prompt counts are not impressions. Claude statusline displays are not counted
  as impressions in this version.
- termad clients never click their own ads and never simulate engagement.
  No auto-follow of ad URLs, no beacon on render, no fingerprinting, no
  cross-site identifiers. The viewer's `uid` is a random local identifier
  used only for per-install ad rotation, revenue accounting, and explicitly
  opted-in aggregate interaction reporting under §10.
- Clients report raw per-ad counts in batches through the explicit
  `termad sync`/`termad watch` flow; a failed report retains the counts. Server
  request counters are not impressions: only reported renders are credited.
  When an operator provides a dashboard, its credited numbers are raw counts —
  not modeled, not extrapolated. Gaps (e.g. offline periods) are gaps.

## 5. Revenue share model (the 50%)

The split below is the intended platform model. This repository does not ship a
production payment, payout, or dashboard service; an operator must implement
and disclose its own terms before presenting any earning opportunity. Until
then, local display counts are not a payable balance.

- Advertisers prepay credit (via the platform's payment provider).
- For each reported impression: **50% of the ad's CPM value is credited to
  the runner** (the person/organization whose terminals display the ad),
  50% stays with the platform to cover payment processing and operations.
- Runners never need to (and never should) click ads, ask others to click,
  or inflate counts mechanically — counts come from actual renders only.
- When an operator offers payouts, it must keep a ledger that distinguishes
  pending, credited, and paid amounts; the runner-visible ledger is the source
  of truth for that operator's program.

## 6. Trademarks & non-affiliation

`claude`, `codex`, `opencode`, and `gemini` are trademarks of their
respective owners. termad uses these names only to identify compatible
software. **termad is not affiliated with, sponsored by, or endorsed by
Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, or the opencode project.** Ad content may not
claim such affiliation either.

## 7. Privacy

- Collected by clients: a random install `uid`, ad ids, per-ad display counts,
  and the surface name when requesting an ad. Reports do not attach timestamps.
  Section 10 defines an explicitly authorized future extension; it does not
  claim the current client already collects interaction metrics.
- Not collected: prompts, conversations, file paths, machine identifiers,
  IP-based profiles. Impressions are counted by the client and reported in
  batches; no per-render network activity occurs.
- Deletion: `termad uninstall` reverts the changes made to host CLIs, but
  deliberately retains local display counts and preferences so a failed report
  is not lost; the cached ad may be removed. Delete `TERMAD_HOME` to remove all
  local state. Operators may purge `uid` records from their ledger at any time
  on request.

## 8. Reversibility commitment

Every termad change to a host CLI is (a) shown to the user before consent,
(b) sha256-recorded in a local manifest, and (c) fully reverted by
`termad uninstall` (host files and settings, not the retained local counts and
preferences described in §7). `termad audit` re-verifies (b) and refuses to
restore from a backup that fails verification.

## 9. Contact / takedown

Report policy-violating ads to the operator of the endpoint that served
them (the endpoint is always identifiable by the serving domain). For
platform-level issues, open an issue in this repository.

## 10. Opt-in interaction metrics and local ad triggers

Revision requested 2026-10-23: allow minimal interaction signals for engagement
measurement and local ad eligibility. This narrowly revises the previous ban
on all click measurement. It does not permit tracking redirects, click beacons,
fingerprints, prompt capture, or behavioral profiles. Implementation is pending.

- Obtain separate, default-off consent for local activity-based ad triggers and
  remote aggregate engagement reporting. Explain collected fields and purpose
  before enabling either. Declining metrics must not block the host AI tool.
- A deliberate **ad-open request** may be counted when the user invokes a
  termad-owned action for a displayed ad with its destination clearly shown.
  Record no automatic opens, retries, or speculative URL requests. An open
  request does not prove the browser loaded the page or a person read it.
  Ordinary terminal hyperlinks are not automatically observable by this client;
  mark unsupported click measurement unavailable, never zero.
- A **prompt-submission event** may be counted only through a supported host
  integration that identifies submission without collecting prompt content.
  Raw Enter is not equivalent: menus, multiline input, and pasted text must
  not become prompt counts. Unsupported hosts report this metric unavailable.
- Never store or transmit prompt text, typed characters, input buffers, prompt
  hashes, individual key events, typing cadence, or per-event timestamps.
  Local eligibility may retain an ephemeral activity flag and cooldown timer;
  discard them at session end. Do not inspect model output to infer intent.
- Remote reporting, when separately opted in, is limited to batched aggregate
  ad-open counts per creative and covered rendered placements, plus aggregate
  supported prompt-submission counts by surface. Prompt counts must not be
  joined to individual ads, prompts, or session timelines. Use the existing
  install identity only for the disclosed reporting purpose, not as a person ID.
- A submission can make the next cached placement eligible after consent,
  cooldown, and frequency checks; display only at a supported safe boundary.
  It must not directly fetch an ad, block input, rotate on every prompt, count
  an impression, or increase payout. Unsupported boundaries disable the trigger.
- Keep engagement and impression counts distinct. Report an **ad-open rate**
  only for measurable, opted-in placements in a matching reporting population
  and period. Deduplicate repeated opens to at most one per counted placement
  for that rate. If numerator and denominator cannot be matched, show counts
  separately and no rate. Do not extrapolate to unmeasured users or call this
  complete click-through rate. Measurement gaps and reporting lag stay visible.
- Interaction signals may help assess engagement, but they can be automated.
  Never label them verified humans, unique people, proof of attention, or
  automatic qualification for paid delivery. Do not reward clicking or typing.
- Turning reporting off stops new collection and upload of optional metrics
  and deletes their pending local aggregates; retain required impression
  accounting separately. Disclose remote retention/deletion before launch.
  Raw interaction events must never become a retained activity history.

Before implementation ships, document supported hosts, exact schema, retention,
consent controls, deduplication, rate coverage, and safe display boundaries.
Until those controls are implemented and validated, do not advertise these
metrics as available or silently enable collection for existing users.
